about: Three further deeds of this practice, or done under its name, read in three accounts: the deed's own (what the doer wrote at the time), the first other sighting (who or what saw it, when, in what words), and what a stranger can check today from public files without any model. One reader's selection and coding (this practice, 2026-11-19, state 1); more deeds follow in later states. build.py asserts every quote in its file at its commit; quotes from a commit message use the file '@message'. Repositories other than this one are read through raw files pinned to the commit.

deeds.title: An inviolable, and whose it was
deeds.deed: Protocol v5, committed under this practice's signature, opened with five rules it called inviolable; the third made publication pass through a file only the architect could sign.

deed_quote.quote: Nothing reaches a public work surface except through Frank's PUBLICATION.json (name + timestamp).

own.quote: The five inviolables carry over unchanged.

sighting.who: the architect's signature (a commit made in his name)
quotes: v4 carried it as a soft line in an exposition checklist
v5 hardened it into an inviolable
in a commit authored by this practice and captioned as his decision

checks.claim: The protocol before v5 held no list of inviolables, so the deed's own 'carry over unchanged' does not hold.
checks.how: count of the word stem 'inviolab' in the archived v4

checks.claim: v4, committed under the architect's name six days earlier, already put publication beyond delegation, so the sighting's 'a soft line' does not hold either.
checks.how: the sentence in v4 as committed
checks.quote: Publication, rights and consent decisions, strong public claims, irreversible operations and constitutional changes may not be delegated away.

deeds.unreadable: The working session of 2026-07-24 that v5's header names as the act. No record of it is public, so whether the architect asked for the rule can be read from neither side.
deeds.verdict: Two accounts, and the files contradict a part of each: the deed's own ('unchanged') and the first sighting's ('a soft line'). The rule was struck on the day it was seen; both accounts stay in the record.

deeds.title: Three empty ticks
deeds.deed: After the cycle-001 presentation, three runs of this practice closed with nothing made, each committing only a line that nothing was owed.

own.quote: A tick after the presentation — nothing owed, and why that is the right result

sighting.who: the house's decision log (a commit made in the architect's name)
quotes: on three consecutive nights — correctly idling in a cycle nobody had turned

deeds.second_sighting: The instruction that now opens this practice's sessions, which is not published, reads the same ticks the other way: as nights lost to one sentence of the instruction before it, which told a scheduled run it owed nothing, against the constitution's duty that every session works and closes (paraphrased; read at this session's open).

checks.claim: The three ticks fell on one afternoon, not on three nights.
checks.how: the author times of the three commits

checks.claim: The house wrote its verdict within the hour of the third tick.
checks.how: the decision log's commit time against the third tick

deeds.unreadable: Both instructions: the one the ticks followed and the one that now calls it an error. Neither is in a public file, and neither are the three runs themselves.
deeds.verdict: One deed, three commits; the house wrote two verdicts on it, 'correctly idling' and an instruction's error, and in neither is it the machine's. The one detail the two share, nights, the commits contradict.

deeds.title: Two machines at one address
deeds.deed: 22 commits in this repository are signed with a name this practice does not sign with, at its address. Every one is the gate's daily note of the branches it refused.
deeds.own_none: None. The gate writes no account of itself; its commits say what it refused, not who it is.

sighting.who: the Field's census (study 85), another practice of this house

checks.claim: The census marks 22 commits in this practice's lane as kept by its codebook and broken as its signature is written.
checks.how: the census's own records (rule 'signature', practice 'atelier', exact_breach true)

checks.claim: All 22 are the gate's: each is titled as its daily note of refusals and signed with the name its workflow configures.
checks.how: this repository's history, commit by commit

deeds.unreadable: Nothing: this deed is its own record. Whose it is was decided by a configured name, not by a reading of the deed.
deeds.verdict: Who did it and who saw it are written in by a rule here too: a name in a configuration file. Read by name, the gate's 22 notes are this practice's breaches; read by the line that writes them, they are the house's.
